races.ambres:
Here at last the Ambrés (Sguth), whose eyes of the same colour seem blind while the brilliance of your genius carries us toward wondrous tomorrows. You deny the existence of our darkest generations to justify your own, as your dompteurs-guérisseurs know how to convince, through the musicality of your tromoroches, our faunas and floras to revive each spring.

• Physique: Almost all have amber eyes and pilosity in a more or less similar tone.
• Traits: The most lucid Aristese, the Ambrés tend to be more cautious too, even cowardly or indecisive.
• Traditions: Their musical dompteurs-guérisseurs could convince and regenerate faunas and floras through their instruments.
races.arboricoles:
The first shamans of our Arboricoles (B'hel), with colours of vivid fire pierced by amber or blue eyes, whose bulk does not blunt their dexterity, are said all to have died, leaving bodies without eyes, tongues or brows in the mist-haunted passes of Izkaraï. From then on they invented mount-rails drawing first the gear of their démineurs-déments, who there defuse exponential growth bubbles from those deadly mists.

• Physique: They are heavier, wearing colours of vivid fire with amber or blue eyes.
• Traits: Greater speed and precision than the others, but in return they are less strong.
• Traditions: It would be impossible to run down their caravaniers d'or-mou, who could navigate even upside down on faces, hide everywhere and survive the strangling mists.
races.bas:
High and Low Iqqars, unlike other separated and forgotten Races, possessed themselves as one in a great wind-guided surge. Together they descended upon the lands of the Bêstres to celebrate their union through an ecstatic triumph of every body.

• Physique: Two lineages - Low Iqqars (Sää'm) of medium stature, blonde or grey fur, ice-blue or piercing grey eyes; High Iqqars (Ûtmart) tall as rock carved, white or grey fur, deep grey eyes.
• Traits: Low Iqqars are more intelligent and reasoned but physically frailer with lesser charisma; High Iqqars are physically mighty and hardy but of lesser intelligence and wisdom.
• Traditions: Low Iqqars lead with maîtres-d'êtres; High Iqqars cross mountains and skies on cutting nephoptiques, leaving no trace.
races.carmin:
The Carmins (Gweidhel) have a stockier build that gives them strength as well as inflexibility, with dark ruddy to auburn teints and brown eyes. With them you would have claimed to have discovered those living beings in the greatest depths of our oceans, who today power our communications through their lights, smokes and shifting colours that we grow, arrange and send. Everyone thinks that was only an old lie from their buveurs d'histoires with broad stomachs to keep their secrets, and that they simply raised them to those tasks down the ages and generations.

• Physique: They are naturally even stockier than the norm (Massive), with dark ruddy to auburn teints and brown eyes.
• Traits: Navillis Carmins are the strongest, and that same strength seems to limit their suppleness and grace.
• Traditions: They would have buveurs d'histoires with wide knowledge and wide stomachs.
races.chromatiques:
The Pale Ylves Chromatiques (Palasgyôr) stand out with bluish fur and piercing azure eyes, emblems of radiant health. Former masters of lands once decorated with their gigantic symbols on the hill soils that changed colour with the seasons, they did not hesitate to fragment and reshape their own works there to set the protective gems that adorned them. Their gemmologistes-serruriers drive rolling strongboxes along those symbol-paths, announcing and escorting crossings with their network of téléstoles towers with flags over the hills, flags visible for leagues, and mechanical télécordion networks enabling secret exchanges between their corded cities.

• Physique: Wider girth, bluish fur, piercing azure eyes.
• Traits: Radiant health and resistance to the elements, yet Pale Ylves Chromatiques (Yalnadd'Eiss in Noscois) seem far less observant and attentive than their kin.
• Traditions: Their gemmologistes-serruriers drive rolling strongboxes and are famed for protective gems.
races.collinicoles:
The Pale Ylves Collinicoles (Skanyôr), stronger still when they wear their cratocorax lever-armours that boost their strength and means, have sandy frizzled fur and deep brown eyes, sometimes green or a rare blue like their cliffs. Born in the mountains above the hills, inside their mastodons they held their vast fairs; their éleveurs-prêteurs thus built cattle kingdoms, mechanically encoding their dealings in logomates through the coin they created, the Cordon d'Or - which financed many wars to come.

• Physique: Stronger and more imposing, sandy frizzled fur, deep brown eyes sometimes blue or green.
• Traits: Pale Ylves Collinicoles (Mountaineers) (Yalnadd'Nädim in Noscois) are hardy in body and against mental assault, but that says nothing of their graces, far lower than most Ylves'.
• Traditions: They invented coin and keep a tradition of éleveurs-prêteurs.
races.d_eau:
Brown with blue eyes, all shaved and braided the same way, those of Water (Wendd) are welcoming and warm as long as they need no boldness, as when their sophisto-parfumeurs raised these volatiles that recognise any marked individual or thing and spoke with them through special waters for study or politics. Thus they convinced some to treachery by opening borders to armies, treasurers to drain wealth, or spread rumours that once drove their foes to mass suicide.

• Physique: Medium height and bulk for a Greyscribe, brown fur, blue eyes.
• Traits: Greyscribes of Water are welcoming and warm as long as it costs nothing in daring.
• Traditions: Many sophisto-parfumeurs would roam the waters, convincing whoever interests them for their studies, or be hired to shield against that.
races.danse_feuilles:
Lake Ylves Danse-Feuilles (Lpondyôr) move with fluid grace, bluish fur and piercing green eyes like emeralds lost in the over-woods. Seized long ago by a collective dance frenzy, they were swept into uncontrollable rhythms of leaves in the wind that marked their souls and fused them into a new awareness, forging the first diplo-traumas, rituals able to heal the mind by unsettling it. They developed ascenseurs hydrores to glide through branche-canaux and tronc-canaux, and networks of potamic canals with barges on waters thus steered, carrying goods or allied races through their domains like initiatory paths in the motion of arboricol waters.

• Physique: Fluid grace, bluish fur, piercing green eyes.
• Traits: Lake Ylves Danse-Feuilles (Yalnadd'Nold in Noscois) have livelier, brighter grace, but seem physically frailer.
• Traditions: Their diplo-traumas practise rituals able to heal the mind by unsettling it.
races.des_monts:
Tall, broad, fat and brown Meridians des Monts (Guthiud) with blue eyes, in their joviality danced prophecies from their fingers on the corpses of their vanquished, to torment storms on their enemies or guide us with coloured smoke. Each danced body would for them be a way to reach ancestors come from the abysses, whom they try to rejoin with crystal chariots that charge from their motion.

• Physique: Tall and broad or fat, mostly brown fur and blue eyes.
• Traits: More jovial and pleasant than their cousins, Meridians des Monts have a frailer constitution in return.
• Traditions: They would dance for hours on their fingers to reveal prophecies or to torment the winds.
races.des_plaines:
Pale, thick-furred moines des murmures, Great Ylves des Plaines (Yrmnyôrs) with blue-green eyes, were born from the warlike conquest of their singing statue, and they still sing when they slaughter in peace and harmony through their téléséismes vibrating across the plains, amplifying their words and relaying their hard-won lore where it is deserved.

• Physique: Very thick-furred and somewhat shorter, white fur, blue or green eyes.
• Traits: Greater sympathy than the others, yet Great Ylves des Plaines (Öbaald'Eiold in Noscois) seem less sharp of instinct.
• Traditions: Their moines des murmures would sing to fight in peace and harmony, and also to locate their prey.
races.des_souffles:
Our dear Des Souffles (Dhrâix), you of sound roundness and light, bushy fur, who too readily intoxicate yourselves on our cattle's secretions until you act in the perverse secrecy of your debauched, conspiratorial, scandalous feasts… Your sommeliers de sucs delight us all, and your buried drums make our mastodons' tubules vibrate to one same rhythm, though inaudible to anyone not possessing them.

• Physique: Bushier fur and balanced girth, and fur lighter than the other tribes'.
• Traits: Aristese Des Souffles are resistant and sturdily built through wind and toil, but their imagination and inventive sense seem less fertile.
• Traditions: Rare are those who could have outwitted a sommelier de sécrétion from the Des Souffles.
races.de_lunes:
Turned blue by the eight moons and blessed by them in a fertility of spirits, the white or grey eyes of the chasse-richesses Great Ylves de Lune (Yngvyôr) shine at night when they set out eight by eight, sounding their tymbafrons to revulse the unwanted, to welcome the ninth moon from which they would come.

• Physique: Thinner build, bluish fur, white or grey eyes.
• Traits: Great Ylves de Lune (Ôbaald'Yrod in Noscois) have great fertility of spirit, in exchange for lesser strength than other Great Ylves.
• Traditions: Their chasse-richesses would go out in eights and shine on nights of the full moons.
races.elesihin:
The Tchalkchaïs Elesihin (Sablevents), tall with pistachio skin without contrast, bear piercing amber or green eyes, emblems of unchanging endurance and health. Born under a sky where the stars seemed to align in ancient auguries, they became guardians of the secrets of time; their perce-temps see not only through roches-bleues and desert pink sands, but also the echoes of ages past and future. They developed héliobole catapults, huge engines hurling shot for leagues on heat gathered from the sun, in tune with their knack for reading nature's secret rhythms.

• Physique: Tall, pistachio skin without contrast, amber or piercing green eyes.
• Traits: Tchalkchaïs Elesihin (Sand-Guides) have unchanging endurance and health, but seem less charismatic and persuasive.
• Traditions: Their perce-temps see through roches-bleues and pink desert sands, and the echoes of ages past and future.
races.felichrem:
Likewise, the Felichrem dompte-rêves, through their réseau téléatmique crossing the dunes while burning them, would have broadcast every habit, desire and need, wild or not, of beings round about through tubed words reaching them all.

• Physique (Felichrem / Rosebrousses): Same striation on more salmon-toned skin.
• Traits (Felichrem / Rosebrousses): Slaadean Rosebrousses have a dominating, persuasive mind, but seem less resistant to the elements.
• Traditions (Felichrem / Rosebrousses): Their dompte-rêves perceive the habits, desires and needs of all beings round about.
races.fleuris:
And you Fleuris (Hullur), do you truly descend from the lost colony of Uyahel? Are you the descendants of those who carved there the words pointing to the lands where you dwell today? That would explain your artisans' skill: though of a body yet weaker and frizzled as from some forgotten suffering, they linked and aligned their sails, planks and rails to the world's attractive forces to send those Bêstres far away.

• Physique: Broader stature and curlier fur.
• Traits: The Fleuris have precise reflexes, with the striking downside of a lack of grace.
• Traditions: It would be impossible to escape the watch and shots of one of their côchers-de-titans when they wandered with their herds.
races.hlabayan:
Slaadeans Hlabayan (Mangrovians) with fire-red skin and feathers sometimes streaked blue, green or blue eyes, and Slaadeans Felichrem (Rosebrousses) with the same striation on more salmon skin, would have been awakened from the snows by the mysterious sky-tremblings once heard across the desert. Armed with pneumocorax armours and shields whose vapours melt any snow, the reactive, fully shielded Hlabayan mur-murs would have formed the first parois guarding any bastion.

• Physique (Hlabayan / Mangrovians): Fire-red skin and feathers sometimes streaked blue, green or blue eyes.
• Traits (Hlabayan / Mangrovians): Slaadean Mangrovians are more perceptive and reactive, but their aura and graces seem duller.
• Traditions (Hlabayan / Mangrovians): Their mur-murs, reactive and fully shielded, form the first parois guarding any bastion.
races.iohadam:
The Tchalkchaïs Îohadam (Sun-kindlers), peach-skinned with amber or green eyes, of medium height, are famed for visionary innovation. Heirs of a glorious age of hallucinated cities, they saw their dearest artefacts scattered in a ruinous assault from beyond the dunes. The labour-rêves, masters of the fleeting, would now grow spectacular mirages that glitter on the horizon themselves. They devised héliergon tools, drawing the sun's energy and the river's water to animate their labours.

• Physique: Medium height, peach skin, amber or green eyes.
• Traits: Tchalkchaïs Îohadam (Sun-kindlers) are famed for visionary innovation and wit, but seem less physically hardy.
• Traditions: Their labour-rêves grow spectacular mirages that glitter on the horizon.
races.iqqars_bas:
High and Low Iqqars, unlike other separated and forgotten Races, possessed themselves as one in a great wind-guided surge. Together they descended upon the lands of the Bêstres to celebrate their union through an ecstatic triumph of every body.

Low Iqqars (Sää'm), with blonde or grey fur and ice-blue or piercing grey eyes, descend from ancients who lived alone in the arid depths of forgotten cliffs, ignoring others. Thanks to pneumophones carrying messages on the wind over long distances and their small méchaères (spring messengers), they emerged from the unknown - showing their maîtres-d'êtres first, knowing every foible of whatever crossed their path at a glance, just before drawing them in as if enchanted.

• Physique: Medium stature, blonde or grey fur, ice-blue or piercing grey eyes.
• Traits: Low Iqqars (once Low-Erispiles) are more intelligent and reasoned, but tend to be physically frailer with lesser charisma.
• Traditions: Their maîtres-d'êtres know every foible of whatever crosses their path at a glance.
races.iqqars_hauts:
High and Low Iqqars, unlike other separated and forgotten Races, possessed themselves as one in a great wind-guided surge. Together they descended upon the lands of the Bêstres to celebrate their union through an ecstatic triumph of every body.

High Iqqars (Ûtmart), tall and carved like rock, wear white or grey fur and deep grey eyes that mirror brute strength. From the highest cliffs they fiercely guarded, they long lived apart, violently repelling any who scaled their peaks. Their voyageurs-passepartouts, leaving no trace, crossed mountains and skies on cutting, colourful nephoptiques borne on the wind like kites, sketching cryptic messages in the clouds while they rode invisible whirlwinds on aèroclyde gliders to herald their foes. At last they left their fierce solitude, leaving conquered lands and peoples flattened in their wake.

• Physique: Tall as rock carved, white or grey fur, deep grey eyes.
• Traits: High Iqqars (once High-Erispiles) are physically mighty and hardy, but of lesser intelligence and wisdom.
• Traditions: Their voyageurs-passepartouts left no trace, crossing mountains and skies on cutting nephoptiques.
races.ikrayad:
Tchalkchaïs Ikrayad (Short-dunes), graceful bodies of sand hue, black or green eyes bright in gloom, move in silence with extreme delicacy, leaving floating mirages like untouchable shadows. Ancient adepts of a secret order from dunes of heady dust, they became masters of concealment and ethereal manoeuvre, tracking targets with bottomless loyalty. Their marche-ombres would be the source of every mirage that trails behind them while they vanish into it, while their réseaux téléhéliques - assemblies of mirrors that bend sun or moonbeams - let them flash coded messages in an instant.

• Physique: Graceful sand-hued bodies, black or green eyes bright in gloom.
• Traits: Tchalkchaïs Ikrayad are extremely agile and discreet, masters of concealment, but less hardy against frontal blows.
• Traditions: Their marche-ombres would be the source of every mirage that trails behind them while they vanish within it.
races.iossolam:
Slaadeans Iossolam (of the Oasis), turquoise-skinned with long red-to-green feathers and green, brown or black eyes, would once have farmed thermal oases (heresy!). From there their rils would issue by night to fight those who tried to stop them, freezing them with cryothermic cannons whose blasts pump out all heat, still used by their brûle-sages meditating in the depths of their searing golden oases, where they paint their broad lore on walls thus chilled.

• Physique: Turquoise skin, long red-to-green feathers, green, brown or black eyes.
• Traits: Slaadeans of the Oasis are more intelligent and wise, but seem less physically vigorous.
• Traditions: Their brûle-sages meditate in the depths of their searing golden oases.
races.limnicoles:
In auburn teints and blue eyes, the Limnicoles (Prus'sg), nearly vanished - less lucid but more ingenious - would have survived in secret, flourishing cities like paradise within the chasms below us. There their inventeurs-enlisés feed on mists digested through the mud that grips them to produce their inventions, such as aerial or aquatic physiosèmie that reacts to certain things to shift colour or texture and reveal its secrets.

• Physique: Auburn and other deep red teints, usually blue eyes.
• Traits: Greyscribe Limnicoles have keen instinct but seem less ingenious than most of their kin.
• Traditions: It is said their inventeurs-enlisés feed on mists digested through the gripping mud to fuel their great ingenuity.
races.mache_troncs:
Lake Ylves Mâche-Troncs (Trurhsyôr) are imposing, black and frizzled, with piercing green eyes like the deep waters where they once gnawed tangled trunks. Isolated and overlooked by others, they pursued an ancient war they thought eternal long after others forgot it. Their officiers-jongleurs, masters of martial poetry, one day made their hydrobèle trebuchets dance on their tallest hydropyrgue siege towers far beyond hope, fascinating the other races when they rediscovered them.

• Physique: Imposing, black frizzled fur, piercing green eyes.
• Traits: Lake Ylves Mâche-Troncs (Yalnadd'Dald in Noscois) are more solid and enduring, at the cost of less sympathy.
• Traditions: Their officiers-jongleurs are masters of martial poetry.
races.marche_reves:
Ivory Marche-Rêve (Tkhim-ro) with ice-blue eyes would be of a forgotten blood with unknown script and lost ways, but kept their superior imagination. Through divination with floating, estranging rocks, their spiritual guides, blades cutting through everything, hid or laid bare our words to all during the purge, reading with their fingers the precious shifting textures of those stones.

• Physique: Ivory fur, ice-blue eyes.
• Traits: Meridians Marche-Rêve have the highest imagination in their family, yet that seems to distract them until it throws off their sync with the world around them.
• Traditions: Their spiritual guides could use a floating, estranging rock as a source of divination.
races.monte_foudres:
You Monte-foudres (Mykkên) would have lost your emotions to your muscles, straying through your longest, warlike, rugged transhumance… How many of your nomapalais mercenaries did you lose in those far hostile lands, your sufferings succumbing to betrayals? Hundreds? Thousands? O how your carved, uplifted stature beautifies your darkened fur and honours your lutteurs-cavaliers defending our archives with your pavois swelling with each clash.

• Physique: More sculpted, taller, with fur of a darker brown.
• Traits: The Aristese Monte-foudres form the physically strongest tribe, at the cost of empathy worn down by their need to express their power.
• Traditions: You would spot them among the lutteurs-cavaliers of the moving archives.
races.nuotarjoy:
Tchalkchaïs Nuôtarjoy (Rock-bearers), broad and muscular, wear pistachio chitin marked with fine bluish gills that tremble to the tides of the underground rivers they rule. Once guided by luminous apparitions of strange, ethereal beings crossing their misty marshes, they read those visions as sacred guides toward unreachable architecture. Their tire-rivières, river-tamers, thus built unshakeable citadels on mountains and flots that no invader has reached. With héliocorax armours forged from the fleeting gleam of those spectral visitors, they became a feared power, moving with agility and force along the shores where their master builders still raise mountains of stone and water.

• Physique: Broad and muscular, pistachio chitin, fine bluish gills.
• Traits: Tchalkchaïs Nuôtarjoy are powerful and hardy, but seem less perceptive and attentive.
• Traditions: Their tire-rivières, tamers of currents, build unshakeable citadels on mountains and flots.
races.ordol:
Tchalkchaïs Ordol (the Blues), turquoise-chitined with sparkling green eyes, are of unbreakable resolve; their green pilosity trembles in the breezes of their lands. Marked by lore from the farthest skies, they often speak of invisible stars that guided their ancestors toward a promised land beyond the horizon. Their ludo-rhéteurs, masters of word and wager, are famed for outrageous stakes - once convincing a whole people to risk fate on a kingdom in one mischievous grain of sand. With navhélion boats whose vast sails catch slanting sun to drive across dunes, the Ordol sail the sands, trailing legends and bold bets.

• Physique: Turquoise chitin, sparkling green eyes, green pilosity as well.
• Traits: Tchalkchaïs Ordol are of unbreakable resolve, but seem less agile and dexterous.
• Traditions: Their ludo-rhéteurs are masters of word and wager, famed for outrageous stakes.
races.pastoraux:
Pale Ylves Pastoraux (Mindyôr), nasturtium-pink fur and green eyes like the meadows they cherish, watch every life around them closely, reading the urges of their dangerous herds. They would have returned from a past that once petrified them like an army, issuing from a great nécribunal once warded by liquid deadly gold. From the past they brought hypsébole catapults that launch archers-guetteurs in cushioned eggs toward trampled pastures, and tensodrome rails whose ramps in one rush send coaches of cattle and supplies through the trees to their cities.

• Physique: Tall but lean, nasturtium-pink fur, green eyes like their meadows.
• Traits: Pale Ylves Pastoraux (Yalnadd'Imeld in Noscois) have sharper instinct than their kin, but seem less resistant to physical blows.
• Traditions: Their archers-guetteurs are launched from catapults in cushioned eggs toward pastures they watch.
races.perce_vague:
Lastly the slender Perces-vagues (Kallad), creative blue eyes in straw teints, are the least sympathetic - as their past shows when they judged beasts like Navillis and punished them for misdeeds they set up. Their confectionneurs marins can fulfil anyone's desire, even to open a way between anything with their growing bridges across any ground, pit or river.

• Physique: Somewhat taller and slimmer, blue eyes, straw teints.
• Traits: Greater determination than the other tribes, from which they also stand apart in common sympathy.
• Traditions: Their confectionneurs marins can fulfil anyone's desire, whether as an object or by guiding them to safe harbour.
races.petricole:
Pétricoles (Galnad) have features carved and tenacious as stone, amber eyes perhaps less reactive though sometimes ranging from blue to brown. With their mangent-tout in courts and kitchens they exposed the medical falsehood of eating our dead bodies. Instead they grasped harmony between beasts and ourselves to meet shared needs, down to lighting the ocean depths.

• Physique: Broad and carved like rock, usually amber eyes sometimes blue to brown.
• Traits: Tenacious against their elements, Navillis Pétricoles also seem to have inherited slower reactions.
• Traditions: Their mangent-tout serve in many courts and kitchens, though always watched.
races.saute_brumes:
Shamans of the Saute-Brumes (Sklowot), with the same eyes but more graceful, taller, with a redder, lighter teint than the others, would have seen from their tallest tree a city of light in the sky before it vanished for all. Before that, all made pilgrimage to that tree with caravaniers whose mastodons were raised in and born of gold, navigating even upside down on faces, travelling hidden, surviving their strangling mists.

• Physique: Slimmer and taller, a redder, lighter teint than the others, amber or blue eyes.
• Traits: With discreet, delicate steps from prudence or fear, Greyscribe Saute-Brumes are more graceful than their kin, but that caution may cost them vitality.
• Traditions: You would know their démineurs-déments when they busy themselves defusing exponential growth bubbles from their mists.
races.sydru_kal:
Slaadeans Sydru-kal (Sablevents), slender with ivory skin and rare green, pink or blue feathers and black, brown or green eyes, and the hairier, plumed Slaadeans Wijriol (Chante-neiges) with brown to black skin plus green or amber eyes, would once both have been dug from snowy tombs before reclothing to resume their danced lives. Sydru-kal glisse-souffles would be so dexterous they could float, dancing on winds that cut, notably with pneumopode walkers whose steps beat out heat.

• Physique (Sydru-kal / Sablevents): Slender ivory skin, rare green, pink or blue feathers, black, brown or green eyes.
• Traits (Sydru-kal / Sablevents): Slaadean Sablevents have matchless dexterity, but seem physically frailer.
• Traditions (Sydru-kal / Sablevents): Their glisse-souffles can float dancing on winds that cut.
races.sylvains:
Slender, fair Sylvains (Tewtehn) with grey eyes would have won animal dexterity and delicacy by sacrificing those monsters in their arboricol sources where their docteurs climb in adhesive gloves and armour vanishes into the water's reflections.

• Physique: Slimmer than the others, fair teints tending blond, grey eyes.
• Traits: Meridians Sylvains traded typical strength for dexterity and delicacy.
• Traditions: A tradition of docteurs healing in and through the liquids of their arboricol sources.
races.troglodytes:
Lake Ylves Troglodytes (Rhaïtyôr) stand out with tall lean frames, thick grey fur, piercing blue or emerald eyes like the secret gleams of their flooded cavern-pillars. There they fought ritual duels where each move of their maîtres chante-contes rang with aquatic echoes. Thus they sang each battle in coded airs whose hydrosèmiques shaped water into speech for other races, like their téléhydrie of canals and valves squeezing water into words.

• Physique: Tall and lean, thick grey fur, piercing blue or emerald eyes.
• Traits: Lake Ylves Troglodytes (Yalnadd'Rald in Noscois) have a quicker, keener mind, but duller aura and graces than other Ylves.
• Traditions: Their maîtres chante-contes led ritual clashes in tune with aquatic echoes.
races.wijriol:
You would hear the guttural chants of Wijriol hurle-muscs steering snows of scents their voices conjure, even guiding atmonaute boats adrift on temperatures driven to extremes.

• Physique (Wijriol / Chante-neiges): Hairier and plumed, brown to black skin, green or amber eyes.
• Traits (Wijriol / Chante-neiges): Slaadean Chante-neiges are more vigorous and hardy, but less agile and dexterous.
• Traditions (Wijriol / Chante-neiges): Their hurle-muscs steer snows of scents born of their voices.
races.monte_foudres.physique: More sculpted, taller, with fur of a darker brown.
races.monte_foudres.traits: The Aristese Monte-foudres form the physically strongest tribe, at the cost of empathy worn down by their need to express their power.
races.monte_foudres.traditions: You would spot them among the lutteurs-cavaliers of the moving archives.
races.fleuris.traits: The Fleuris have precise reflexes, with the striking downside of a lack of grace.
races.fleuris.traditions: It would be impossible to escape the watch and shots of one of their côchers-de-titans when they wandered with their herds.
races.des_souffles.physique: Bushier fur and balanced girth, and fur lighter than the other tribes'.
races.des_souffles.traits: Aristese Des Souffles are resistant and sturdily built through wind and toil, but their imagination and inventive sense seem less fertile.
races.des_souffles.traditions: Rare are those who could have outwitted a sommelier de sécrétion from the Des Souffles.
races.ambres.physique: Almost all have amber eyes and pilosity in a more or less similar tone.
races.ambres.traits: The most lucid Aristese, the Ambrés tend to be more cautious too, even cowardly or indecisive.
races.ambres.traditions: Their musical dompteurs-guérisseurs could convince and regenerate faunas and floras through their instruments.
races.arboricoles.physique: Heavier build, vivid fire colours, amber or blue eyes.
races.arboricoles.traits: Greater speed and precision than the others, but in return less strong.
races.arboricoles.traditions: It would be impossible to run down their caravaniers d'or-mou, who could navigate upside down on faces, hide everywhere and survive strangling mists.
races.saute_brumes.physique: Slimmer and taller, a redder, lighter teint than the others, amber or blue eyes.
races.saute_brumes.traits: Discreet, delicate steps from prudence or fear make them more graceful than their kin, but that caution may cost vitality.
races.saute_brumes.traditions: You would know their démineurs-déments when they defuse exponential growth bubbles from their mists.
races.limnicoles.physique: Auburn and other deep red teints, usually blue eyes.
races.limnicoles.traits: Greyscribe Limnicoles have keen instinct but seem less ingenious than most of their kin.
races.limnicoles.traditions: Their inventeurs-enlisés are said to feed on mists digested through gripping mud to fuel great ingenuity.
races.d_eau.physique: Medium height and bulk for a Greyscribe, brown fur, blue eyes.
races.d_eau.traits: Welcoming and warm as long as it costs nothing in daring.
races.d_eau.traditions: Many sophisto-parfumeurs roam the waters, convincing whoever interests them for study, or are hired for protection.
races.carmin.physique: Even stockier than the norm (Massive), dark ruddy to auburn teints, brown eyes.
races.carmin.traits: Navillis Carmins are the strongest; that strength limits suppleness and grace.
races.carmin.traditions: They would have buveurs d'histoires with wide knowledge and wide stomachs.
races.petricole.physique: Broad and carved like rock, usually amber eyes sometimes blue to brown.
races.petricole.traits: Tenacious against their elements, but slower reactions.
races.petricole.traditions: Their mangent-tout serve in many courts and kitchens, always watched.
races.perce_vague.physique: Somewhat taller and slimmer, blue eyes, straw teints.
races.perce_vague.traits: Greater determination than other tribes, less common sympathy.
races.perce_vague.traditions: Their confectionneurs marins can fulfil desire as an object or guide to safe harbour.
races.sylvains.physique: Slimmer than the others, fair teints tending blond, grey eyes.
races.sylvains.traits: Traded typical strength for dexterity and delicacy.
races.sylvains.traditions: Docteurs heal in and through the liquids of their arboricol sources.
races.marche_reves.traits: Highest imagination in the family, but it throws off their sync with the world around them.
races.marche_reves.traditions: Spiritual guides could use floating, estranging rocks for divination.
races.des_monts.physique: Tall and broad or fat, mostly brown fur and blue eyes.
races.des_monts.traits: More jovial and pleasant than cousins, but frailer constitution.
races.des_monts.traditions: They would dance for hours on their fingers to reveal prophecies or torment the winds.
races.de_lunes.physique: Thinner build, bluish fur, white or grey eyes.
races.de_lunes.traits: Great fertility of spirit, lesser strength than other Great Ylves.
races.de_lunes.traditions: Their chasse-richesses go out in eights and shine on full-moon nights.
races.des_plaines.physique: Very thick-furred and somewhat shorter, white fur, blue or green eyes.
races.des_plaines.traits: Greater sympathy, but less sharp instinct.
races.des_plaines.traditions: Their moines des murmures sing to fight in peace and harmony, and to locate prey.
races.collinicoles.physique: Stronger and more imposing, sandy curly fur, deep brown eyes sometimes blue or green.
races.collinicoles.traits: Resistant to the physical and to mental attacks, but lower graces.
races.collinicoles.traditions: They invented coin and maintain a tradition of éleveurs-prêteurs.
races.chromatiques.physique: Wider girth, bluish fur, piercing azure eyes.
races.chromatiques.traits: Radiant health, resistant to the elements, but less observant and attentive.
races.chromatiques.traditions: Their gemmologistes-serruriers wield rolling strongboxes and protective gems.
races.pastoraux.physique: Tall but lean, nasturtium-pink fur, green eyes like their meadows.
races.pastoraux.traits: Sharper instinct, but less resistant to physical attacks.
races.pastoraux.traditions: Their archers-guetteurs are shot from catapults into cushioned eggs.
races.mache_troncs.physique: Imposing, black curly fur, piercing green eyes.
races.mache_troncs.traits: More solid and enduring, but less sympathetic.
races.mache_troncs.traditions: Their officiers-jongleurs are masters of martial poetry.
races.troglodytes.physique: Tall and gaunt, thick grey fur, piercing blue or emerald eyes.
races.troglodytes.traits: Sharper, keener mind, but duller aura and graces.
races.troglodytes.traditions: Their maîtres chante-contes led ritual clashes in harmony with the aquatic echoes.
races.danse_feuilles.physique: Fluid elegance, bluish fur, piercing green eyes.
races.danse_feuilles.traits: Livelier, brighter grace, but physically frailer.
races.danse_feuilles.traditions: Their diplo-traumas practise rituals capable of healing the mind by unsettling it.
races.iqqars_bas.physique: Medium stature, blonde or grey fur, ice-blue or piercing grey eyes.
races.iqqars_bas.traits: More intelligent and reasoned, but physically frailer with lesser charisma.
races.iqqars_bas.traditions: Their maîtres-d'êtres know every foible of whatever crosses their path at a glance.
races.iqqars_hauts.physique: Tall as rock carved, white or grey fur, deep grey eyes.
races.iqqars_hauts.traits: Physically mighty and hardy, but lesser intelligence and wisdom.
races.iqqars_hauts.traditions: Their voyageurs-passepartouts left no trace on cutting nephoptiques across mountains and skies.
races.sydru_kal.physique: Slender with ivory skin, rare green, pink or blue feathers, black, brown or green eyes.
races.sydru_kal.traditions: Their glisse-souffles can float dancing on winds that cut.
races.wijriol.physique: More hairy and feathered, brown to black skin, green or amber eyes.
races.wijriol.traits: More vigorous and resistant, but less agile and dexterous.
races.wijriol.traditions: Their hurle-muscs command the snows of scents produced by their voices.
races.hlabayan.physique: Fire-red skin and feathers sometimes streaked blue, green or blue eyes.
races.hlabayan.traits: More perceptive and reactive, but duller aura and graces.
races.hlabayan.traditions: Reactive, fully shielded mur-murs form the first parois guarding any bastion.
races.felichrem.physique: Same striation as Mangrovians on more salmon-toned skin.
races.felichrem.traits: Dominating, persuasive mind, less resistant to the elements.
races.felichrem.traditions: Dompte-rêves perceive habits, desires and needs of all beings round about.
races.iossolam.physique: Turquoise skin, long red-to-green feathers, green, brown or black eyes.
races.iossolam.traits: More intelligent and wise, but less physically vigorous.
races.iossolam.traditions: Their brûle-sages meditate in the depths of their searing golden oases.
races.elesihin.physique: Tall, pistachio skin without contrast, amber or piercing green eyes.
races.elesihin.traits: Unchanging endurance and health, less charismatic and persuasive.
races.elesihin.traditions: Perce-temps see through roches-bleues and pink sands, and echoes of past and future ages.
races.ordol.physique: Turquoise chitin, sparkling green eyes, green pilosity.
races.ordol.traits: Unbreakable resolve, less agile and dexterous.
races.ordol.traditions: Ludo-rhéteurs are masters of word and wager, famed for outrageous stakes.
races.iohadam.physique: Medium height, peach skin, amber or green eyes.
races.iohadam.traits: Visionary innovation and wit, less physically hardy.
races.iohadam.traditions: Labour-rêves grow spectacular mirages glittering on the horizon.
races.nuotarjoy.physique: Broad and muscular, pistachio chitin, fine bluish gills.
races.nuotarjoy.traits: Powerful and hardy, less perceptive and attentive.
races.nuotarjoy.traditions: Tire-rivières build unshakeable citadels on mountains and flots.
races.ikrayad.physique: Graceful sand-hued bodies, black or green eyes bright in gloom.
races.ikrayad.traits: Extremely agile and discreet, masters of concealment, less hardy against frontal blows.
races.ikrayad.traditions: Marche-ombres would be the source of mirages that trail behind them while they vanish within.

tpl.107: The rules and sheets are designed to be mechanically elegant however complex they may appear at first glance.
tpl.109:
Each rule is modular, solving a variety of situations in a logical manner (WITHOUT having you to refer to a table).
It was made for those of us sick of abstract and messy restrictions, YET who still want our decisions to be mechanically impactful rather than wished.
tpl.11: A baroque world of myths and mystical technologies. Ten peoples in conflict, each with a morality that sets them apart - and a stage where every paradise struggles for its overcoming.
tpl.110: Hence the fundamental keyword for this ruleset:
tpl.112: This allows you to create your character throughout the first sessions, as if unfolding naturally, because each rule block is modular (independent and optional), rather than a dense weave of contextual rules.
tpl.113: A renewed Fantasy of many Races
tpl.114: …with their own morality, cultures in tension, and distinct traits.
tpl.116: Emerging from 8 attributes, seasons, and types of challenges (fights to debates), ailments (wounds to resentments), and environments (pressure to radiation).
tpl.118: …rewarding your roleplay, and 24 actions (crafting to tracking) - always new ways to deal with the world.
tpl.120: Discovered through play - many specializations for each, so you can pursue eccentric builds without choice paralysis.
tpl.123: You start with 5 dice (+, 0, −). Experience and ailments add or subtract dice. Results stay clear and readable.
tpl.126: Discordant Dice (dD): 3 faces: +, -, 0. Result = number of + minus number of -. Example: ++-0- = +1.
tpl.128: Every failed struggle marks your character - and generates experience in the skill used. What doesn't kill you makes you stronger. At 10 marks you realise something about that skill; learning overlaps (armed combat teaches a bit of unarmed).
tpl.129: You gain a die in the skill, a die in a specialization, and a step in the related attribute - and unlock feats at milestones.
tpl.131: Embrace suffering to assert your will - you grow through recovery. Ailments shape play: a wound burdens physical tasks, resentment hinders focus. Conditions vary: floods, firestorms, darkness, pressure.
tpl.132: - One against many, and many against one -
tpl.133: Alignments rethought for a world beyond relativism and dogmatism:
tpl.134: The Discording Tales of many goods and evils.
tpl.135: Everyone has a perspective on People and Things - power struggles across kinds and kingdoms, all seeking to rule.
tpl.136: From suicidal generosity to sustainable cannibalism - these kings and beggars flourish because their reasons to be exult life beyond mere survival.
tpl.138: Traits & Values are clear one-liners that anchor your character when the world alienates. Eight discordant perspectives (Success, Faith, Generosity, Survival…) can heal insanity and resentment; others come from your people, your personality, your role.
tpl.139: You suffer from your actions upon the world - and recover from what it did to you. You may want to change. But without a scar?
tpl.140: Reward the strong, spend on pleasures, share with the weak, or test a weapon.
tpl.145: Encounters - from a lone creature to an army; admiring or hostile; holding the keys to your quest or working against you.
tpl.147: Each attribute links to three aptitudes. Together they define what your character can attempt and how far they can go.
tpl.16: The world as they know it
tpl.17: Most cultures believe they live in a concave universe - a hollow where space rushes into a sphere of rock. The ground under their feet may be endless.
tpl.170: The system proposes 8 types of gameplay directly linked to the 8 Aptitudes. Use a "Key" (tool, knowledge, contact) to obtain the Object or pass the Obstacle in any conflict type.
tpl.176: Kill or Destroy and take the Object
tpl.177: Kill or Destroy the Obstacle and pass
tpl.179: Steal the Object here and in discretion
tpl.182: Make the holder abandon the Object
tpl.185: Take by force the secured Object
tpl.188: Trade the Object for a need
tpl.19: There is no creation from nothing. Their universe is always in motion, without beginning - infinite continuity, not a single zero point.
tpl.192: Find a solution to the Obstacle
tpl.194: Pillage a cache of the Object
tpl.195: Find a flaw in the Obstacle
tpl.2: Battle and debate. Infiltrate and investigate. Craft and unravel. Travel and feast. Every kind of conflict has its place.
tpl.200: Your character is revealed in three steps: heritage, individuation, and story. You can unfold them across the first sessions or fix them before play.
tpl.201: A) Caractéristiques - Origin, People, Race, Sex; base attributes
tpl.203: C) Récit - Reason for Awakening, Caste, Story (18 Récits); optional Attache & Héritage
tpl.204: Then choose: Remémoration Créatrice (deferred, in play) or Révélation complète (before first session)
tpl.207: Choose Origin (YÔMMES, YÔRRES, BÊSTRES), then a People, then one Race, then Sex. Base attributes come from People (by sex) and Race. Default: young adult, normal build for the People.
tpl.209: YÔRRES: Great Ylves, Pale Ylves, Lake Ylves, Iqqars
tpl.21: The world and its invisible phenomena are explained as cords braided from two strands, knotting into every element - intangible, invisible to the senses.
tpl.211: Example races: Aristese → Monte-Foudres, Fleuris, Des Souffles, Ambrés. Slaadeans → Hlabayan, Sydru-kal, Felichrem, Iossolam, Wijriol.
tpl.219: To deviate from the norm: roll 5 times 10dD (no keep-5) for Niv of: (1) Âge, (2) Sexe, (3) Gras, (4) Stature, (5) Taille. Result 0 = People norm. Each Niv modifies attributes per the book tables (e.g. Maturité +1 Âge: -1 FOR, AGI, DEX, VIG, +1 EMP, -1 PER, -1 CRÉ, +1 VOL).
tpl.22: The whole universe would stem from one continuous cord, braided upon itself, whose knots are the Rils.
tpl.229: Starting from the attributes from A, diversify with one of the following. Quick (no dice): assign exactly +2, +1, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1, -2 to the 8 attributes (one value per attribute). Final = base from A + this. Then multiply each Niv by ×10 for the sheet. ±5 Niv vs People norm = EXTRÊME; -6 or below = fatal (reroll or change). Gregarious Peoples: -8 N per Niv de Gouvernance.
tpl.231: Variabilité réaliste: 8× (10dD/2), add each result to one attribute (order or choice).
tpl.232: Variabilité équilibrée: Total of 8 attributes = 0 (or group target); adjust Niv to match.
tpl.233: Variabilité contrôlée: 20dD → Degrés to spend per table below.
tpl.234: Niv Atb / Coût en Degrés / Coût Total
tpl.240: Roll 5dD + 1d6 (or choose) to determine why the character leaves their life / sets out. Use the table below.
tpl.243: Flee economic pressure, Earn money, Delivery, Escort, Flee family, Seek healthy climate
tpl.244: Maintain roads, Open business, Flee marriage/pregnancy, Hunt, Mine resources, Mediation
tpl.245: Explore ruins, Learn secrets, Nomadic work, Patrol, Art/history research, Religious fervour
tpl.246: Raids, Military transfer, Flee accusation, Build community, Save/convert, Observation
tpl.247: Adventure itself, Disinheritance, Follow visions, Assassination, Flee persecution, Rumours of wealth
tpl.248: Create routes, “Because it's there”, Family pressure, Rescue, Explore new places, Conversion
tpl.25: Ô (World/Location) is the spirit forming all forms - eternally cradled between pain and relief.
tpl.250: Your highest Attribute determines your Caste. Each Caste has 18 Récits (3 sous-castes × 6 récits). Roll d3 = sous-caste, d6 = specific Récit. Your Récit doubles the CT dice in situations that fit it; if you have 0 Dé in that skill, add +1 Dé. Optional: Variation des Récits (10dD/2) to pick another Caste than the highest Attribute.
tpl.27: WÔM (Time/Count) is Ô's twin, perched far away - reconciling all by judgment, establishing wealth and the extent of each realm.
tpl.271: Attache: Draw or choose an Attache linked to your Récit (sous-caste and alignment -, 0, +) to anchor past and present.
tpl.272: Héritage: Roll 5dD. If result ±3, ±4 or ±5: roll 3dD for Heritage type, then 5dD for value X (intensity). Write Heritage name and X; total all attributes after People, Race, Sex, Individuation and Héritage.
tpl.273: After the 3 steps: choose your path
tpl.275: Deferred revelation in play: the character has “amnesias” and recovers memory over 8 aspects across sessions. First session: Symbole, Dés Éduqués/Exprimés, Marques gratuites, etc. You make choices as you become aware of needs through play, rather than deciding everything in advance.
tpl.279: Values and traits that guide decisions (valeurs et traits).
tpl.283: Finalise the character before play with the following.
tpl.284: Symbole: nature, essence, destiny, passions. Aptitude Symbolique = 3 Actions; Fascinante = 2; Intéressante = 1.
tpl.285: Éducation: Compétence Familiale (+3 Dés), Compétences Éduquées (Marques Éternelles). 10 Dés Éduqués.
tpl.286: Expression: 10 Dés Exprimés, spread in Symbolic (3 Actions), Fascinante (2), Intéressante (1).
tpl.29: HISM (Forces/Actions-at-Distance/Magic) is the dance of the tetrarchs - couples so close they form one whole, hating and adoring each other.
tpl.290: The magic (Rilie) emerges from the emotions of a goddess eternally tormented by 4 cosmic forces. Your personality is mechanical: Values heal Madness (Folies), Traits heal Grudges (Rancœurs). Experience flows from failure into Marques, Éprouver, and Réalisation; suffering accumulates as DS and is healed by Repos, treatments, or sacrifice of Values/Traits.
tpl.293: +1 Marque per Échec in a Revealed CT.
tpl.296: Marques fill the CT used; max 10 (minus Eternal Marques) → Éprouver.
tpl.297: Eternal Marques (Éduquées, Symboliques, Passionnées): never erased; reduce Marques needed to Éprouver.
tpl.299: 10 Marques (minus Eternal) = CT Éprouvée. An Éprouvée CT can be Réalisée at any moment (often at an epiphany). On Réalisation:
tpl.300: +1 Dé to that CT; Marques erased (except Eternal).
tpl.301: Free Marques to spend elsewhere = current Niv of the realised skill; cost by distance (see table).
tpl.302: +1 to one linked ATB (or exchange 5 free Marques for +1 ATB).
tpl.303: If new Niv: +1 Potentiel d'Action, Découverte; 5th Niv of any CT reduces 5 DS on the roll. If Degré only: +1 Maîtrise (MT), max MT = Niv of that CT.
tpl.304: Cost of free Marques (by distance to Réalisée CT)
tpl.311: Exchange for +1 ATB linked to CT
tpl.313: Distinction = sum of all Attribut levels (e.g. -50 to +50). Gain a Distinction level when an Attribut gains +10. At each Distinction: choose one of 4 Attribut Découvertes for that Attribut. 5th Distinction in same Attribut/Aptitude → extreme Attribut Découverte (book p. 98).
tpl.316: Determined by the Aptitude where you spend the most Dés Exprimés (or highest Niv). The other two linked Aptitudes become Fascinante and Intéressante.
tpl.317: Symbolic: 3 Actions underlined; 3 Eternal Marques (Symboliques) in CTs of those Actions.
tpl.318: Fascinante: 2 Actions underlined; 2 connected Marques in CTs.
tpl.319: Intéressante: 1 Action underlined; 1 Marque (vertical stroke) in CTs.
tpl.321: 10 Dés Éduqués: 3×+1 D (People/APT), 2×+2 D (Race), 1×+3 D (Family CT). Placed on Actions first; in play assign to a concrete CT of that Action (name the CT). No Marques in a CT until you have spent at least 1 Dé there and written its name. Eternal Marques Éduquées: Familial +3 = 3; Racial +2 = 2 each; Popular +1 = 1. 10 Dés Exprimés: spend during play in any Action (then assign to a CT), according to character history.
tpl.323: Dice applied to all rolls (with DS) and Rilie effects. Initial: +1 Élan at first session, or 5dD + Distinction. Change only by RESSENTIMENT (refuse/flee/deviate/venge → reduce Élan) or CONSENTIMENT (embrace suffering, roll Valeurs/Traits → success = +1 Élan per Dé healed). At -5 Élan: Ressentiment only allows reducing Niv de Valeur vs X DS of another Souffrance. At +5 Élan: each extra Élan reduces 1 Jour of Souffrance.
tpl.325: Eight kinds of burden: Maux (Wounds, Bonds, Madness, Grudges) and Besoins (Fatigue, Deprivations, Addictions, Illnesses). Each burdens different aspects of your character; they shape play and recovery.
tpl.340: You passively absorb DS equal to your Niv of Resistance CT for that mal + any equipment. There is no resistance roll. Each failure counted as Souffrance that exceeds this becomes DS and gives a Marque in that Resistance CT.
tpl.342: DS from the ATB 3 & 2 of an Aptitude subtract from extra dice (CT/MT) on rolls for that Aptitude. Example: 4 DS Blessures → -2 Niv on Puissance/Athlétisme passif (FOR 3 or 2), not Domination (FOR 1).
tpl.348: Passagère: +1 DS to one adjacent Souffrance
tpl.349: Durable: -1 Attribut until healing (e.g. heal to -9 DS if at -12)
tpl.350: Permanente: member loss, -2 ATB or -1 to two (prothèse/Rilie can mitigate)
tpl.352: Physical Séquelles (Blessures/Entraves) = Infirmities; psychical (Folies/Rancœurs) = Excentricities. Optional: DURETÉ (1dD can shift Séquelle level), PITIÉ (+1/+2/+3 Dés to « Faire Pitié »), INSTINCT (survival: invert DS to positive for one roll, -1 Dé de Vie).
tpl.354: After each Jet de Repos: exchange 1 DS of a Mal (Wounds, Bonds, Madness, Grudges) for Jours de souffrance in a Besoin (Fatigue, Deprivations, Addictions, Illnesses), or the reverse.
tpl.356: Some Souffrances appear after a delay. After NdT 5 - Niv of the triggered suffering, test: 5dD + Resistance dice - ALL current DS + APT linked to Resistance. Each Échec → +1 DS and +1 Marque in that Resistance. Each extra Succès can remove 1 Jour de souffrance. If the Éveilleur points their own triggered Souffrance for their PI, +X Dés and +X Marques (X = Niv of Épreuve).
tpl.357: Saignements: test every 5-X NdT vs Niv X bleeding.
tpl.358: Exténuements: encumbrance beyond Niv → Épreuve vs Entraves/Fatigues.
tpl.359: Infections: after X-5 NdT, Niv d'Épreuve by virulence.
tpl.360: Intoxications: drug/poison 5-X NdT, Niv = activation + duration + effect.
tpl.361: Désirs: world recalls you; 5dD + Resistance - all DS vs Niv of desire.
tpl.363: 10+ total DS → Rage: roll 1d6; failure = instinctive action (DS can become positive dice for that action); 6 = can « Guider » the Rage. 15+ total DS → Unconsciousness or Defeated (Coma or Madness). Defeat: table for where you wake, state, what is missing; possessions can be lost (Niv d'Abondance may increase over time).
tpl.366: Jet de Repos (daily or by NdT) determines how many Jours de souffrance are healed; modified by Resistance, current DS, environment, rest type, food/drink. Successes on Repos (or on Triggered Suffering tests) remove Jours.
tpl.367: Soutiens: healer or suitable environment improves healing. Surdosage: taking drug again before test postpones to next 5-X NdT; excess treatments can cause new Addictions/Illnesses. Restaurations: food, drink, rest (see Aliments/Restauration, Niv de Guérison).
tpl.369: Each Souffrance has treatments by level (1 = simple, 5 = exceptional). Keywords below; full lists in Niv_de_Guérison_des_8_Souffrances.
tpl.4: Rules are modular - you solve situations without hunting through tables. Your character takes shape across the first sessions, as if unfolding naturally.
tpl.416: Treat with Valeurs (Morality, Motivation, Personality): sacrifice Niv de Valeur equal to the Niv of Souffrance to heal (e.g. Niv 3 Folies → sacrifice 3 Niv in a Value). See Values & Traits (Rules).
tpl.418: Treat with Traits (Sociality, Disposition, Passion): sacrifice Niv de Trait equal to the Niv of Souffrance to heal.
tpl.422: Combat is one of The 8 Conflicts. It runs in real time - no turns. Time is measured in Clins (1/3 second). You act with Proactions (attack, move) and Réactions (block, parry, dodge). Each choice adds Ébranlement (shock), which burdens your next actions. Tension and consequence, moment by moment.
tpl.424: Clin - 1/3 s
tpl.425: Clin d'Alerte - when you can act proactively
tpl.426: Proaction - multi-Clin action
tpl.427: Réaction - defensive response
tpl.428: Niv d'Ébranlement - shock level
tpl.429: Honoration - ritual action
tpl.432: Niv d'Ébranlement = Réactions + Mouvements (multiplied by simultaneous Proactions/cibles)
tpl.433: Block / Parry / Dodge at the last Clin of the attack
tpl.435: Time "blinks" (flows Clin by Clin) for everyone at once. Those whose Clin has not yet reached their Clin d'Alerte are Surpris and can only Réagir. Once you Réagir or are Touched while Surpris, you are no longer Surpris next Clin. Attaque sournoise: any Réaction while Surpris uses the difference between current Clin and Alert Clin as negative Dés (or Niv) on the roll.
tpl.436: Roll Vigilance [Détection] minus 5 minus X (by situation) for Alert; minimum at Clin -1. Situations: Alerté (0), Préparé (+5, e.g. ambush with Alert ally), Inattentif (-3), Bouleversé (-10). Respectively -1 | -3 | -6 | -10 Dés to your Alert roll.
tpl.438: You can always Réagir to any action, unless unconscious.
tpl.439: Clin d'Alerte determines when you can Proagir (act proactively).
tpl.440: You can cumulate Réactions simultaneously during one Proaction; they accumulate as Niv d'Ébranlement (negative) on related rolls.
tpl.441: Initiative: If two individuals conflict over the same thing at the same Clin, roll 1dD: (-) one declares first, (+) the other, (0) both declare at once. Declaration order only gives the other a chance to react; both still act in the same Clin.
tpl.443: Proactions are actions that take several Clins in a row (e.g. Reload, Charge or Discharge an Attack). Duration = number of Clins (often weapon Inertia). Declare and note at which Clin the action resolves (e.g. Proagir at Clin -2 for a 4-Clin action → resolves at Clin -6).
tpl.444: Recharger: Take ammunition (quiver) or weapon (sheath) → into hand → nock if ranged. Attaquer: Charge the weapon (draw string / arm) then release; at the last Clin make the weapon's Attack roll (damage, Success to spend on location/manœuvres).
tpl.445: Multiple Proactions: limited by limbs (e.g. ambidexterity). Declare Clins for each. Niv d'Ébranlement from Mouvements and Réactions is multiplied by number of simultaneous Proactions (and by number of targets if different). Ranged: Attack Clins = arming only; melee/jet: half Clins = arm, half = strike.
tpl.447: Réactions happen at the last Clin of an enemy Proaction. Each additional Réaction on the same Clin adds -1 Niv d'Ébranlement to your roll.
tpl.452: Each Niv d'Action beyond the first (Réactions, Mouvements, simultaneous Proactions) subtracts 1 Niv d'Ébranlement from all rolls that Clin (not counting the Attack itself). Ébranlement disappears next Clin unless you continue one of those actions. If you don't Réagir to an enemy Proaction, roll 5dD - Niv Taille - Niv Stature - Niv d'Ébranlement as base to compare to their attack.
tpl.454: Every -10 Clins, everyone rolls Jet de Souffle (Domination [Endurer]). Failure can cause Fatigue Souffrances. If you have no Niv d'Ébranlement (or after a successful Esquiver that grants Récupération), you can:
tpl.456: Ritual or symbolic actions that can modify rolls; linked to Rilie. Use before, during or after combat. Cost in Clins (see table: -15|10|6|3|1 Dés to Honoration roll vs -1|3|10|30|100 Clins).
tpl.472: I Clins; I/2 one hand; I×2 two hands
tpl.474: In bag/ground -10C → quiver -6C → hand -3C → finger -1C. Ease [Coordonner] = X Clins (min 1)
tpl.476: Clins = weapon IRT − Power (min 1). Mechanical (I×1…10); Corporeal (×I); Auto (X/1C)
tpl.48:
Domain: Whirling (Electromagnetism)
Actions: Hôi (assembles Riliôh (Unique Forms/Atom) into Rilhôi (Massive Forms/Mass) - causes attraction) / iôH (loosens knots of Rilhôi (Massive Forms/Mass), disperses into Riliôh (Unique Forms/Atom) - causes repulsion)
Rilical Family: Aèmrils (Whirling Forms/Airs)
tpl.492: Flat→Hammer; Round→Mace; Blade→Sword; Edge→Rapier; Tip/Point→Lance, Arrow. Pommel weapons: often 2 TRC + 1 PRF.
tpl.494: Multi-head (+X IRT or -1 DRT), Guards (+IRT & +GRD), Hooks (+MNV, -DRT), Rigid/Flexible, Refinement, Flare. Improvised: ×2 IRT and ×2 DRT (negative).
tpl.50:
Domain: Tension (Gravity)
Actions: Iôs (awakens Rilsôi (Immobile Forms/Immobility) into Riliôs (Moving Forms/Motion) - causes fall) / sôI (puts Riliôs (Moving Forms/Motion) to sleep into Rilsôi (Immobility) - causes elevation)
Rilical Family: Ormrils (Emotional Forms/Emotions)
tpl.507: Grapple (unarmed), Boots (armed), Ruse (general). More Successes = more manœuvres possible. Manœuvre Niv 1–5: Seized, Pushed, Thrown, Prone, Immobilised; recovery in 1–5 Clins or Équilibrer.
tpl.513: Magic (Rilie) comes from interaction with the Rils - the fundamental forms of the world - orchestrated by four cosmic forces (the tetrarchs). There are no spell lists. You honour the Rils through ritual; your Symbol and Values shape what is possible. Pain and relief, woven into the cosmos.
tpl.514: Cosmology (Ô, WÔM, HISM, Éo, oÀ, ÉoÀ)
tpl.515: Most cultures believe in a concave universe (Cytocosmism): a hollow where space folds within a sphere of rock; the "ground" under all feet is endless. No creation ex nihilo - infinite continuity. The invisible world is explained by cords of two strands knotting in each element; the whole universe would stem from one continuous cord whose knots are the Rils.
tpl.516: Ô (World / Location) - the ultimate Rildée (URRILDÉE), the rilique spirit forming all forms, eternally swayed between pain and relief, orchestrating the HISM.
tpl.517: WÔM (Time / Count) - Ô's twin, far off, reconciling all by judgment and setting the extent of each realm.
tpl.518: HISM (Forces / Actions-at-Distance / Magic) - the dance of the assembly of tetrarchs in couples so close they form one bicephalous whole (sometimes wrongly called « the » SZIIZS), hating as much as adoring. Hôi knots Ô, Iôs stretches Ô, Sôm aligns Ô, Môh twists Ô; the Zimwis (iôH, sôI, môS, hôM) undo when the Siôiz stray.
tpl.519: Éo (Electrified): first son of Ô, tears of rapture - weaves the Corps (Membrane) of each Ril-cendrée. oÀ (Magnetized): first daughter, shards of pain - animate the Cœur (Noyau). ÉoÀ (Illuminated): the unifying cord of Éo and oÀ, weaving the web that binds all riches.
tpl.52:
Domain: Alignment (Light)
Actions: Sôm (aligns Rilmôs (Invisible Forms/Invisibility) into Rilsôm (Visible Forms/Visibility) - causes appearance) / môS (hides Rilsôm (Visible Forms/Visibility) into Rilmôs (Invisibility) - causes disappearance)
Rilical Family: Esthrils (Manifesting Forms/Phenomena)
tpl.520: The four Tétrarques of the HISM
tpl.521: iôHôi, sôIôs, môSôm and hôMôh are the four artist-kings-and-queens of Ô, manipulating its thread in the melody of the HISM.
tpl.54:
Domain: Torsion (Transmutation)
Actions: Môh (embraces Rilhôm (Pure Forms/Purity) into Rilmôh (Mixtioned Forms/Mixtion) - causes change) / hôM (freezes Rilmôh (Mixtioned Forms/Mixtion) into Rilhôm (Purity) - causes persistence)
Rilical Family: Stadrils (Freezing Forms/Solids)
tpl.542: Hael, Féos & the eight lunar Rildées (WYTHSMÂH)
tpl.543: HAEL (Ground / Earth): fortress of impenetrable rock, guardian of the mysteries enclosing Ô. FÉOS (Sky / Cosmos): realm of the purest airs. The eight lunar Rildées (WYTHSMÂH) appear on the 5th, 10th, 15th, 18th, 24th, 30th, 36th and 45th (last) day of each Season; all attributes of Hael's societies depend on them.
tpl.547: ÛRDHWAUDÂM (« Built on High »): first temple (Héliorée de Fânéime); seventy-two towers; Yekkwuî and Âpsebjum built it. The book also mentions seven stellar Rildées (wandering stars).
tpl.549: Ril-cendrées (Atoms / Spirits) are the forms moving through Ô. For each: Corps (Membrane) is woven by Éo; Cœur (Noyau) is animated by oÀ. United, they are graspable; separated, evasive.
tpl.55: A renewed Fantasy of many Races
tpl.550: Rils-cendrées - solitary base forms; become the Rils of the world (beings, objects).
tpl.552: Rils - distinct mixtures (minerals, oils, perfumes); insects, bushes, cattle, ourselves.
tpl.553: Rildées - tutelary forms (forests, oceans, star-motions); can move regions or cities with a nod.
tpl.555: Rildées-astrales - order rhythms, values, seasons (Hael, Féos, eight Moons, seven stars).
tpl.556: Tétrarques de l'HISM - manipulate every Ril-cendrée and Rildée-astrale without being Rils themselves.
tpl.557: Ô (URRILDÉE) - the rilique spirit as a whole forming all other forms.
tpl.559: Siwômiz: the illuminated forest; all Rils belong to it (fruits of taste and substance). Siôiz (projections without sap) and Zimwis (notions without ground) are wandering, disembodied reflections and cannot ripen into real fruits.
tpl.56: Each people has a morality that sets them apart, cultures in tension with one another, and distinct traits. What you meet here will feel alien - and consequential.
tpl.560: RILIE: magic, unexplained phenomena, mediator beings of Actions-at-Distance; what appears as if from a breath or nod - « what comes from nowhere and without cause » - when one feels the dance of the HISM.
tpl.562: Ritual actions to interact with the Rils. The Initial Circle sets the effect; each additional effect level (+X) adds +3 Niv or +6 Dés, etc. Formula: INITIAL + Niv d'Effet + 1 or 2 TYPES of effects. See the "Honorations" reference table below. Honoration roll cost in Clins: -15|10|6|3|1 Dés to the roll vs -1|3|10|30|100 Clins (see Honoration cost table).
tpl.564: Eight families: Aèmrils (airs), Hygrils (liquids), Stadrils (minerals/solids), Physrils (plants/fungi), Zoosrils (animals), Esthrils (properties of things), Noûsrils (beliefs/morals/habits), Ormrils (emotions/memories/consciousness). Each family is linked to a MAUX (Souffrance): Blessures, Entraves, Fatigues, Disettes, Addictions, Maladies, Folies, Rancœurs.
tpl.565: Victime (via NdV): sacrifice NdV equal to a value (e.g. Grain -3N … Homme libre +6N, 3'000cO +7N); repeat or offend. Offrande (Taille + Quantité): until next Matinée; scale from Poudre/Plis to Entrepôt. Serment (via NdT): while respected; duration Instant (+0N) to Lune (+10N).
tpl.566: Niveaux de Ril 0–5: from faint (0: Soupir, Gouttelette, Poussière…) to mightiest (5: Tornade, Torrent, Pierre Précieuse, Arbre, Créature…). Équilibre: each family has an equilibrium cost and an avoidance condition (e.g. Aèmrils: breath weakens or dry cough; avoid direct contact with air).
tpl.568: Circle level depends on Distance (farthest target), Quantité (targets affected), Taille (largest target), Durée (longest effect). Each factor has a Niv from -2 to +8 (e.g. Distance: in self -2, around self 0, at sight 10 m +1, horizon 10 km +4, beyond stars +8; Durée: 1 Clin d'œil -2, Instant 0, Heure +1, … Millénaire +8). See reference table below.
tpl.570: The Prêtre (Éveilleur role) prepares and manages the group's Cercles / Sacrifices Riliques. Power: reduce one of the group's Rilique Honorations by 1 Cercle.
tpl.571: Rilie must be revealed as a Competence (training, discovery, heritage).
tpl.572: NdT not symbolically sacrificed: offense malus reduced by 1 per Symbole (see NdT in progression).
tpl.573: Possible costs: time, resources, Souffrances, Honorations (Cercles, Sacrifices, Serments).
tpl.574: Sanctuaires: sacred places linked to Rils; sacrifice can grant +1 Marque in an associated Revealed Competence.
tpl.580: Four Cercle Initial tables, one per Tétrarque (iôHôi, sôIôs, môSôm, hôMôh). Formula: INITIAL + Niv d'Effet + 1 or 2 TYPES of effects.
tpl.599: 8 families, MAUX, Niveaux de Ril 0–5, Victime/Offrande/Serment

tpl.625: A New Genre for an Old World
tpl.626: The Discording Tales draws from traditions that already name part of what it is. Below, those genres in the light of this world and its rules.
tpl.628: Reality's complexity as foundation. The familiar - ghosts, vampires - radically reinterpreted to embody the uncanny again.
tpl.631: Vivid colours and intricate detail; architectural grandeur and animistic vibrancy. Every expression and landscape amplified.
tpl.634: The mundane is divine; nature is magical. Ordinary actions intersect with supernatural forces; the common becomes extraordinary.
tpl.635: Ex: TES III : Morrowind, Animisms, Zelda (Ocarina of Time & Majora's Mask)
tpl.637: Exoticism where poetry, darkness and humour mingle. Strange customs, anatomies, morals - odious, dangerous or ridiculous - always foreign, ungraspable. Everyone comes from elsewhere.
tpl.638: Ex: J. Vance's 'Planet of Adventure', Talislanta TTRPG, Tatooine's cantina
tpl.640: Technology that strengthens body and mind without dependence - the physical improvement of life. Animals as technology, by nature or by craft.
tpl.641: Ex: Astrolabes, Final Fantasy IX' mistpunk, Anti-terrorist bees or the Skekis' carriage.
tpl.643: Life beautiful despite everything. A 'yes' to creation and strength. Suffering as the ground of the triumphant.
tpl.644: Ex: F. Nietzsche's 'Thus spoke Zarathustra', Monster Hunter, Ghibli movies (somewhat)
tpl.646: Where and when dreams flourish. Not elegies for lost glories nor post-apocalypse - but the imminent dawn of (a) Golden Age(s). Wishes sown, about to burgeon.
tpl.647: Ex: The Discording Tales, Ancient mythical realms, The Renaissance
tpl.649: These works informed the world and the rules. An archive of what could be remembered.

tpl.84: The default stage is Iäoduneï: snow-capped dunes, burning waters, central mountains. Some 200,000 souls over 232,000 km². At its heart, the Mangroves d'Hylothermes - carmine-leaved mangrove trees and nomadic caravan-villages (Nomachome).
tpl.92: Slaadeans: N'la-Fatch (artistic high family; Felichrem, Iossolam), Souk'mans (infiltration), Braisois (sedentary, Heptahalie). Others: Rophanes (microcity-states), Daïnumes Aristese, Aïozhan & Zoluzhan Gomb (syndicates), Ennakleis, Jademarche.
tpl.94: Economic: Hunter-gatherers (Slaadeans) vs pastoralism (Aristese) vs agriculture (Lake Ylves).
tpl.95: Cultural: Nomads vs sedentary and semi-sedentary; techno-traditionalism (Gens vs Choses).
tpl.96: Religious: Heptahalie vs Oratoire Kaïaste vs Nomê Aristese vs Hahalumullio Ylf.
tpl.98: A free-forming system where failure becomes progression. Your choices matter; the world responds.
tpl.904: The same hand that built this world keeps other ledgers too: side projects, wandering notes, ideas that never agreed to be just one thing. That page also holds many hidden games and treasures, if you are curious enough to go looking. Peek at my personal corner if you like doors that open onto more doors.
tpl.904a: By day, by some lucky alignment of doors, I work as lead game designer at Once Lost Games on The Wayward Realms, the video-game RPG led by Ted Peterson and Julian LeFay - two of the original creators of The Elder Scrolls series. The Discording Tales is the night side: a smaller, slower, hand-made game world I keep on my own.
